meta.storyTitle: Complete the shared external Node runtime foundation

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Complete the shared external Node runtime foundation

summary.prose: Bundle and dev installations will share one verified Node distribution stored independently of application releases. A read-only resolver binds every installed launch to the manifest runtime identity; bootstrap and preparation acquire missing runtimes through the existing controller lock. Application and IDE payloads contain no Node or Ollama distributions or archives. This correction supplies S4's runtime prerequisite without implementing daemon lifecycle or migration behavior. Current acceptance and S4 handoff cover macOS/Linux only, following the user's explicit Windows deferral. Windows technical contracts stay documented, but its native qualification, ownership prerequisite and target enablement remain deferred and cannot be credited from POSIX evidence. Manual-review rework restores one full application integrity proof per install/upgrade/recovery operation, isolates writable build tools, and explicitly states the same-user runtime and publisher trust boundaries. Ordinary production deadlines are fixed; qualification chooses slow budgets only through an explicit trusted context. Round2 correction makes corrupt-entry recovery explicitly manual and unenforced, with a precise diagnostic and accepted concurrent-use risk. The proposed macOS/Linux store removes write bits to prevent ordinary accidental writes, while preserving writable isolated build inputs and the existing same-user trust limit.

api.name: privateRuntimePaths
api.signature: privateRuntimePaths(location: InstallationLocation, identity: RuntimeIdentity, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal | undefined }): Promise<ResolvedPrivateRuntime>

parameters.name: location
parameters.purpose: Explicit installation-home trust boundary; no global PATHS import or ambient home selection.

parameters.name: identity
parameters.purpose: Exact manifest identity, including target/baseline, pinned archive digest and relative executable.

returns.meaning: Frozen exact-identity result: identity, directory, node, npmCli, headers and inventorySha256; Windows nodeLib included when qualified. This existing unused path-constructor export becomes the single verified read-only resolver.

errors.condition: Wrong policy, executable/target/baseline/npm/header identity, missing/corrupt completion or inventory, changed/missing/extra runtime files.

preconditions: A complete runtime store entry already exists. The resolver never downloads, extracts, repairs, creates directories, acquires controller ownership, changes release selection or opens application stores.
Use only Node builtins and installer-only schemas/policy/lazy native path checks. No src/shared/paths.ts, application entry, DB, provider or source-builder imports.
No arbitrary trusted runtimeDirectory string from a request/receipt is accepted. Exact full Target identity is validated; path segments use validated safe tokens.
Grounding and proposed correction are traced by c1,c2,c7; public/behavioral constraints by c4,c6,c8.
postconditions: Absolute node/npm/header paths are contained in the exact verified distribution; no PATH, tools/node, legacy layout or process.execPath fallback.

Verify bounded receipt/inventory against release-owned pinned distribution inventory digest; verify each selected file's digest/size/mode and exact tree membership once per resolution. No application/Ollama payload traversal. Consumer may pass this result within the same launch operation, never persist a JS capability as a wire flag.
The change has no known production callers of the former helper; add real consumers in this correction, with S4 consuming it later.

Process-local verified results may be reused only for the same explicit location/full identity within one operation. No global cache or persisted trust flag; each new worker/process independently verifies its runtime before admission.

On macOS/Linux canonical resolution requires protected publication modes: each distribution file equals pinned mode with0222 removed, every entry directory0500 and metadata0400, with unchanged independent inventory/content/execute intent. A writable compatible entry returns the explicit protection-required diagnostic; only the existing controller may verify and remove write bits before ordinary resolution. No source-stage/transition mode is accepted by the resolver or any wire input. (c19)

api.name: renderInstallerBootstrap

parameters.name: platform
parameters.purpose: Render shared manual/IDE terminal script from the same template.

parameters.name: assets
parameters.purpose: Digest-bound control assets and pinned distribution metadata derived from official archives; never ambient runtime overrides.

returns.meaning: Shared bootstrap script with exact runtime/control identities and foreground install-to-TUI handoff.

errors.condition: Unknown/unqualified target, mismatched fixed policy or missing digest-bound control assets.

preconditions: Before using any Node executable, script hashes it against the release-owned nodeSha256 for the pinned distribution profile. Fresh archive digest is verified before extraction/execution.

Cached canonical runtime reuse first verifies that exact node executable with OS hashing, then runs only trusted embedded verifier/control bytes after their digest checks; no receipt-supplied code is executed.
Grounding and proposed correction are traced by c1,c2,c7; public/behavioral constraints by c4,c6,c8.

The target including baseline is required; no implicit baseline. Normalize repeated/trailing home separators before creating stages. Immediately before final handoff, OS-hash canonical Node, bootstrap and native control assets again.
postconditions: No host Node needed. Valid matching runtime/control may be reused offline; missing runtime requires live official download, and missing uncached control assets fail offline.

Fresh bootstrap runtime publication helper holds the same native operation.lock used by managers and exits before final canonical-node manager acquires a fresh lock; the shell/PowerShell waits for that exact child, not PID/kill/file age.
Final manager revalidates controller state and ordinary admission; bootstrap does not transfer an OS handle, manager session or selection authority.

Windows publication never renames/moves the currently executing staged node.exe or loaded native DLL: helper executes from one owned stage and publishes a separate verified copy with native directory publication. Retain the execution stage until exact helper exit.

INT/TERM/HUP during foreground publication are recorded; after observing the exact child's exit, clear active-child state, clean only owned closed stages and return the signal exit status. If exact exit cannot be confirmed retain evidence. A residual same-user race between path hashing and path execution, including ancestor replacement, is accepted; no claim of fd-bound execution.

A SIGTERM/SIGHUP sent only to the shell PID, including a signal between helper_active=1 and child creation, is recorded and is not forwarded. The shell waits for exact helper exit before cleanup; cancellation can take the remaining helper publication bounded by its existing deadlines. Prompt cancellation is supported for foreground-group signals, not promised for shell-only delivery. No background forwarding/kill redesign is introduced. Linux qualification must run real group-signal cancellation under dash as well as preserve the macOS shell evidence. (c19)

parameters.name: protection

returns.meaning: Content/tree/ownership/mode verification only; never path allocation, sealing, repair or a resolved launch capability.

errors.condition: Pinned content, identity, exact membership, execute intent or lane-specific permissions differ.
An owned verifier resource cannot positively close.

preconditions: Existing analyzer-located API; add only the internal lane discriminator, keeping the existingfirst3arguments. (c19,c20)
Read-only canonical resolver always uses published. Controller source-stage/permission-transition checks require its original ownership proof and cannot be reused as a launch result.
postconditions: Official inventory JSON and its pinned hash retain original0644/0755 mode values. POSIX published actualmode must equal pinnedmode&~0222, not merely compare both masks while allowing write bits. Source-stage requires original modes; transition accepts only exact original/protected variants per member while preserving all content/ownership/link checks.

POSIX published entry/distribution/subdirectories are0500, metadata0400, executable files0555 and nonexecutables0444. Source stages remain0700 directories/0600 metadata with original pinned file modes. Windows mode semantics remain deferred/unqualified; this is no native Windows enablement.

dataModelChanges.details: Public RuntimeIdentity remains {version,target,sha256,relativeExecutable}; ReleaseManifest stays schemaVersion1. Extend private src/installer/runtime-policy.json with a versioned deterministic distribution profile and per os/arch archive-derived nodeSha256/inventorySha256, calculated from the verified official archive without executing target bytes. The profile selects node, complete npm subtree and required include/node headers, excludes command aliases/symlinks; Windows includes the official matching arch/node.lib, acquiring a separately pinned official header/library asset if the ZIP lacks it. Pin any such extra asset URL/hash in the same policy and bind it in the profile inventory; do not fake header availability. Policy records are checked into release-owned source and changing their generated values requires qualification review, not an install-time override. archive metadata presence alone never enables a target. The result type is a frozen process-local value, not a serializable authority token. Proposed runtime-only source files src/installer/runtime-store.ts and src/installer/runtime-acquire.ts separate read-only verification from acquisition; src/installer/runtime-policy.ts exposes the existing helper name as the resolver. Pin archive byte counts alongside hashes for exact-size bounded downloads, plus independently verified extra header/library assets where required. (c1,c2,c7)

Canonical root is <home>/runtimes/22.22.1/<os>-<arch>-<validated-baseline>/<archiveSha256>/; distribution/ contains the exact profiled runtime, inventory.json lists path/bytes/mode/sha256, completion.json is a bounded schemaVersion1 canonical private record naming full RuntimeIdentity, profileVersion, policy-bound inventorySha256 and npm/header versions. Inventory hash must equal the release-owned policy value, not merely a receipt-supplied hash. Completion plus inventory do not self-authenticate arbitrary bytes. One home has 0..N runtime entries, each entry owns exactly one distribution, inventory and completion; each application release refers to exactly one RuntimeIdentity; 0..N bundle/dev releases may share it. Installer code never changes published runtime content or removes entries through application cleanup. On macOS/Linux publication removes all write bits: entry/distribution/subdirectories0500, inventory/completion0400, pinned0644 files become0444, pinned0755 files0555. Official archive bytes, original inventory mode records, inventory hash, profile version and completion format remain unchanged. Published verification checks actualmode equals pinnedmode with0222 removed AND rejects any remaining write bits; it preserves exact execute intent, ownership and non-link constraints. This prevents ordinary accidental create/overwrite/unlink in the store, but an owner can chmod, rename an ancestor or retain a previously opened writable descriptor; it is not protection against the same user. Isolated writable npm/node-gyp/header/library copies remain required and restore only the original owner-write/execute intent in the owned build workspace. (c19) Do not add per-release pointer files. Use private current-user ownership/ACL, local filesystem, no symlink/reparse/hardlink/special-file acceptance; no writes from the resolver. Metadata/path/file/tree counts, sizes and runtime I/O have explicit fixed finite bounds in implementation tests. Fixed runtime limits: completion 64 KiB, inventory 16 MiB, 32768 entries, 128 MiB per file, 1 GiB expanded and 256 MiB per compressed asset; reject excess before allocation/publication. Ordinary production network deadline600s and read-only verification120s are fixed finite cancellable runtime-only budgets independent of INSRC_QUALIFICATION_PROFILE, including invalid values. Only a trusted qualifier entrypoint may select existing bounded slow-vm budgets and inject an internal process-local deadline policy; caller input, requests, installed receipts and ordinary env cannot select it. Child qualifier workers need a documented explicit launch-only context installed before importing runtime modules; ambient environment alone is insufficient. No20s full-payload assumption. These caps do not broaden application bundle limits. (c1,c2,c7)

Proposed internal src/installer/runtime-acquire.ts provides controller-owned acquisition using the existing ControllerStore/PreparationLease lock capability; it is not an added public manager action. It accepts validated identity and location plus live owner checks, never wire trust flags or arbitrary runtimeDirectory. Reuse verified matching entry before network. Missing entry: live official HTTPS download under fixed per-asset caps/deadline, pinned archive digest, bounded safe extraction of exact deterministic profile, private stage, Node/npm/header/library/version/target inventory checks, durable receipt/inventory, native exclusive directory publication under operation.lock. Conflicting/incomplete immutable destination is an error and is retained; never overwrite or infer actor death. Bootstrap uses the same policy/profile/receipt validation compiled into a minimal digest-bound control helper: all Node/control bytes verified before execution; helper acquires operation.lock, checks real owner/root, publishes from nonexecuting stage and exits. It does not enroll/select a release or pretend an admitted install finished. Outer script observes exact child exit and starts final manager under canonical verified Node, obtaining ordinary fresh ownership. If installed manager already holds the controller lock, acquisition reuses that original capability and never creates a second controller. Keep staged downloads/network handles closed before cleanup; no new supervisor, PID/kill control or privileged dependency. (c1,c2,c7) Corrupt/incomplete entries remain untouched. Recovery is documented manual guidance only; it has no product command, native lock holder, consumer registry/closure proof, operator-move enforcement or fixture claiming such enforcement. Recommend stopping every consumer/build/installer for this home, preserving the entire corrupt identity directory outside the store, then using the authenticated installer for normal missing-entry acquisition. The product cannot prove this manual precondition or hold operation.lock during the move. Concurrent writers/readers may be disrupted or race the replacement; this residual manual-recovery risk is explicitly proposed for human acceptance. Do not promise safe/locked/positively verified manual recovery. Automated quarantine/replacement and new lifecycle actions remain outside scope. Use InstallerError code runtime-invalid with this exact message template: Shared Node runtime verification failed at "<runtime-entry>": <reason>. This runtime is shared by all releases; no repair was attempted. Manual recovery only: stop all Insrc consumers of "<home>", preserve and move the entire entry outside the runtime store, then rerun the authenticated installer. This procedure is not protected by operation.lock; Insrc cannot confirm that every consumer has stopped. If unsure, leave the entry unchanged and request operator assistance. Substitute only derived canonical entry/home and the failure reason; do not print a runnable arbitrary-path deletion command. The guidance/message and preservation are tested, not an operator move or shutdown enforcement. (c19) Read-only protection stays with the existing verifier/publication owners, with no content repair. For fresh owned stages, verify original pinned source modes/content, remove write bits via owned no-follow handles, fsync permission metadata/directories and verify protected modes before native no-replace publication. For an intact existing unprotected/partially protected entry, the existing controller lock may verify every file/tree/owner against independent policy in permission-transition mode, then idempotently REMOVE write bits and verify strict published form, with no byte rewrite, entry rename, network or consumer shutdown claim. Existing readers remain readable; an overlapping verifier can fail a changed-metadata check and may be retried after protection finishes. Corrupt content/unsafe ownership is retained untouched and receives manual guidance. Read-only launch never chmods; a compatible writable entry instead says exactly: Shared Node runtime is not write-protected at "<runtime-entry>". Re-run the authenticated installer to verify and protect this existing entry; no bytes will be replaced. Partial sealing/durability failure retains evidence with resource-close-uncertain; no launch result or success is returned. Retry of a positively closed permission-only attempt must reverify full content before completing protection; no actor closure is inferred from PID/age/lock absence. Closed owned sealed source stages may restore owner write bits only for discard under the original stage capability, with bounded no-follow identity checks; uncertain stages/canonical entries are never unsealed or deleted by that cleanup. Native harness disposal may restore directory write bits only inside its positively owned isolated home after all actor groups close. This is a permission-only compatibility transition, not corruption repair or a new lifecycle/recovery action. (c19,c20)

dataModelChanges.entity: Application-only bundle descriptor and dev receipt
dataModelChanges.details: Private ReleaseDescriptor schemaVersion2 removes runtimeArchive entirely; manifest.runtime retains exact official identity. PayloadInventory schemaVersion1 is now application-only for descriptor2. Private DevReleaseReceipt advances to schemaVersion2 and its recipeVersion advances for application-only inventory; old receipts/offers remain distinguishable and incompatible, not silently rewritten. All canonical hashing/offer persistence/readers are updated together. App inventory includes runtime native dependencies (e.g. .node modules), bootstrap/manager/TUI and production closure, but no Node/Ollama executable/distribution/archive contributions. Publisher collects the out tree and resolved production dependency closure independently from runtime build/probe inputs. Its actual guarantee is source containment in allowed roots (or exact generated files), rejection of explicit excluded runtime/download roots even after destination renaming, blocked runtime/Ollama paths/basenames, and rejection of known independently pinned archive/executable/header-archive/node.lib digests. It is not a positive executable/package allowlist or proof of the origin of arbitrary bytes. Unknown-version binaries, recompressed archives, copied unpinned npm/header/Ollama library files can evade known-content checks; trusted release source/dependency review remains required. Do not blindly deny per-file common license/vendor JS hashes, which can legitimately occur in application dependencies. Collector opens every regular file through captured traversal identity with no-follow/identity recheck, including single-link files; no late path-only read. Runtime archives may be transient publisher/download/test inputs outside app/IDE payloads. Native qualification, inventory limits, exact source/target/offer hashes and unsafe archive checks remain. Reject old embedded-runtime formats diagnostically; no automatic adoption, migration, uninstall or modification of host v2. (c1,c2,c7)

manager-entry and terminal-entry resolve explicit location plus receipt/policy identity and compare realpath process.execPath to resolved node before control work. Installed manager, daemon launch selection, TUI, Retry, bootstrap and publisher probes all consume the same foundation; no release tools/node selection remains. productionPeers receives the verified result for dependency/toolchain use; S3 runtime readiness uses verified external paths rather than a directory guess. Both bundle and dev preparation resolve/acquire the candidate manifest identity under original manager ownership before destructive lifecycle work and use absolute verified npm/header/node paths; dev payload/publisher omit runtime bytes. No source checkout/npm/compiler is used for installed start/status or receipt resolution. Existing S2 closed-worker/source proof, S3 consent/Retry/retained Ollama and same-terminal TUI behavior remain. This batch does not supply fake lifecycle/migration peers or change manager action gates; S4 T3/T11 consume the runtime resolver after this batch passes. (c1,c2,c7) Current-build execution coverage applies to existing owned bundle/dev, manager/terminal, TUI/Retry, bootstrap and publisher consumers. Main-epic S7 owns the future Windows bridge transport process and its runtime-selection/execution tests; this foundation exposes the resolver for that owner and does not implement or claim to test an absent bridge process. (c13,c14,c15) Full application integrity is a distinct activation/recovery boundary: fresh preparation verifies/extracts every inventory member and yields an operation-local identity-bound proof; manager repeated verify calls reuse that proof only within the same operation. Recovered/newly reopened candidates require one full inventory file hash/exact-tree verification before quiesce, migrations or activation, then reuse it for subsequent checks in that operation. Start/status/readiness/TUI control opening stays bounded and never traverses full application/Ollama payloads. Proofs are neither serialized nor accepted from wire flags or receipts; failed/cancelled or new operations cannot inherit them. Dev and bundle paths follow the same rule; tests truncate non-control modules/addons after preparation then simulate a new recovery operation. Within-process runtime results are likewise passed through when identity/home matches, avoiding redundant resolution; Ollama runtime resolution/binding happens before admission/frame creation/readiness deadline, and a new worker verifies before control work. Bootstrap work is normalized once into a canonical absolute value before parent containment, leaf extraction or any filesystem/transport use; every downstream use takes that value. The foreign archive fixture is described as pinned-size rejection, not target-binding proof; renderer identity and pinned target digests retain target-binding coverage. These are remaining existing-bootstrap-owner corrections after LLD/PLAN approval. (c19)

This ISSUE is standalone and has no formal parent shared-contract entries. External epic c3d71313f34bce71 HLD7 sc1–sc7 are compatibility references only: preserve its public runtime/manifest/manager/dependency/IPC/terminal shapes, keep S4 daemon lifecycle and S5 hook execution owned by their existing stories, and leave action-specific manager gating outside this batch. No shared contract is re-owned or redefined. Local acceptance ac1–ac6 are derived from this approved issue, not new epic FRs. See cited prior ISSUE/HLD/S004 PLAN (c4,c6,c8). (c1,c2,c7) S7 also retains its Windows bridge process implementation and runtime-selection/execution coverage. Its existing approved ownership is not moved into this standalone correction. (c13,c14) Release-owned target execution/publication gating explicitly excludes Windows while deferred, independently of self-declared NativeQualification input. Policy metadata extraction may still inspect foreign archives without execution; qualified-target enabling needs a separate reviewed release-owned change. CI Windows qualification is absent or explicit opt-in default-false; never run it in this macOS/Linux scope.

errorCases.detection: Resolver requires exact policy/full identity, canonical completion and inventory; pinned expected inventory digest plus exact file set/digests/modes/npm/header checks detect absent or changed bytes, including rewritten self-consistent local metadata.
errorCases.response: Retain the corrupt entry unchanged and return InstallerError('runtime-invalid') with the exact recovery message in §4.3. Recovery is operator documentation only: code does not hold operation.lock for the manual move, verify all-consumer shutdown, prevent an operator move or promise safe concurrent recovery. The user must explicitly accept that risk. Test the diagnostic and nonmutation, not nonexistent closure enforcement. (c19)
errorCases.userImpact: A shared runtime failure blocks dependent releases; manual recovery is uncoordinated and concurrent-use failure/data risks are disclosed. If unsure the operator leaves the entry unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: Invalid official runtime download or unsafe archive
errorCases.detection: HTTPS/status/redirect/size/deadline/hash checks run before extraction; bounded parser validates entry paths/types/collisions/links and deterministic profile before executing any target binary.
errorCases.response: Abort, close download/parser handles and clean only the positively owned closed stage; no runtime completion or release selection is published.
errorCases.userImpact: Install/upgrade fails safely; existing runtime/release stays selected.

errorCases.scenario: Bootstrap cached executable or control helper is tampered
errorCases.detection: OS hashing compares exact node bytes and cached control/native assets to independent release-owned expected digests before their execution; receipt cannot supply these expectations.
errorCases.response: Do not execute suspect cached code. Missing entry can be acquired live; conflicting canonical entry fails with diagnostic rather than overwrite. No elevation or unsigned legacy adoption.
errorCases.userImpact: Offline use succeeds only with verified cached prerequisites; missing/corrupt cache yields explicit failure.

errorCases.scenario: Controller is busy/lost or bootstrap child closure is uncertain
errorCases.detection: Native operation.lock acquisition/held checks and original owner assertions bracket publication; outer launcher observes the actual child process exit status, never a PID/file-age heuristic.
errorCases.response: No publish/selection with missing ownership; final manager never starts while publication helper may still own the lock. Retain uncertain stage evidence; do not send kill or infer lock release from close(void).
errorCases.userImpact: Concurrent installation reports busy or uncertain completion; no duplicate controller writer.

errorCases.scenario: Windows publishing attempts to move an executing runtime or DLL
errorCases.detection: Bootstrap contract separates execution-stage paths from publication-stage paths; tests trap accidental equality and native Windows fixture observes directory publication with loaded control DLL outside destination.
errorCases.response: Use the separately verified owned publication tree; native publication failure leaves existing entry untouched and no completion claim.
errorCases.userImpact: No successful Windows install claim without actual native evidence.

errorCases.detection: Private descriptor/dev-receipt schemaVersion and dev recipe discriminator distinguish old semantics before inventory opening or runtime selection.
errorCases.response: Reject with legacy-runtime-format diagnosis. Never reinterpret old receipt, rewrite completed ledger, auto-migrate host v2 or resolve its release-local runtime.
errorCases.userImpact: Old rewrite-test fixtures must be rebuilt in isolated homes; real legacy migration remains S5-owned.

errorCases.scenario: Unqualified target or missing exact dev header/library provenance
errorCases.detection: Full target/baseline native qualification gate plus fixed policy profiles require official pinned Node/npm/header/library files and source metadata.
errorCases.response: Block publication/preparation explicitly. Cross-target inventory extraction may compute metadata without executing target bytes but cannot qualify the target.
errorCases.userImpact: Unsupported routes remain unavailable until genuine platform qualification.

errorCases.scenario: Known runtime contribution contaminates application payload
errorCases.detection: Allowed real source roots/exact generated files, explicitly excluded runtime/download inputs, blocked inventory paths and known independently pinned digests. These checks catch exact known contributions even when destination keys are renamed. They cannot infer arbitrary byte provenance.
errorCases.response: Reject the known or source-excluded contribution. Do not claim unknown-version/recompressed/copied unpinned SDK content is detected or silently stripped; dependency/source review is still required.
errorCases.userImpact: Release assembly enforces its documented known-content/source boundary, not universal distribution identification.

errorCases.scenario: Non-control application member corrupted before recovery/activation
errorCases.detection: New/recovered install/upgrade operation lacks fresh process-local preparation proof, so verify complete inventory/tree and every member before destructive lifecycle steps. Truncated modules/addons must fail.
errorCases.response: Stop before quiesce/migration/activation. Retain candidate/evidence under existing recovery semantics. Reuse successful fresh proof only within the same operation; no serialized trust marker and no repeated full scans on status/readiness.
errorCases.userImpact: Corruption cannot be activated simply because bounded control files still pass.

errorCases.scenario: Runtime publication succeeds but parent directory flush fails
errorCases.detection: Distinguish publication completion from later durability/close steps; wrap unexpected canonical-entry lstat errors in InstallerError.
errorCases.response: Use resource-close-uncertain for postpublication durability/closure uncertainty, retain canonical entry and owned evidence, never overwrite/retry by inference. Classify inaccessible entry as permissions-invalid or runtime-invalid with cause.
errorCases.userImpact: Actionable coded failure identifies uncertain publication and retained evidence.

errorCases.detection: Distinguish changed/unowned launcher bytes from recognized owner whose predecessor is legacy, missing or corrupt.
errorCases.response: Return a specific legacy-runtime-format or launcher-predecessor-unresolvable diagnostic with recovery guidance; do not falsely classify known owned launcher as unrelated, overwrite unknown bytes or claim TUI handoff succeeded.
errorCases.userImpact: Post-install failure explains the actual predecessor condition instead of repeating generic ownership conflict.

errorCases.scenario: Ordinary process inherits invalid qualification selector
errorCases.detection: Production runtime/download modules use fixed constants; they do not import env-selected qualification budgets.
errorCases.response: Ignore INSRC_QUALIFICATION_PROFILE in ordinary control. Only trusted qualifier entrypoint validates/installs explicit bounded context before module import, with typed qualifier error there.
errorCases.userImpact: Stray normal/slow-vm/invalid values cannot change ordinary deadlines or break module loading.

errorCases.scenario: Compatible writable or partly protected canonical runtime
errorCases.detection: Content/identity/tree match independent policy, but strict published POSIX permissions differ. Source-stage/permission-transition verification is internal and does not return a launch result.
errorCases.response: Read-only resolver returns runtime-invalid with the exact protection-required message in §4.3. Existing authenticated bootstrap/controller may verify the complete intact entry and idempotently remove write bits only under its current lock, without network, content rewrite or entry replacement. If content/ownership differs, preserve it and use manual-corruption guidance. Partial protection/durability uncertainty retains evidence and returns resource-close-uncertain.
errorCases.userImpact: Ordinary launches never change permissions or use a writable entry; rerunning the installer can protect intact old entries without replacing bytes.

errorCases.scenario: Attempted accidental write to protected canonical runtime
errorCases.detection: Ordinary write/create/unlink is denied by actual POSIX file/directory permissions; strict verifier separately rejects restored write bits or changed bytes.
errorCases.response: Keep canonical data unchanged; build tooling writes only to its owned writable SDK copy. Same-user chmod, ancestor replacement and previously opened writable descriptors remain outside this protection, explicitly accepted rather than called immutable security.
errorCases.userImpact: Known build writes work in isolation; accidental canonical writes fail instead of poisoning every release.

edgeCases.input: Matching verified runtime used by multiple bundle/dev releases, including offline reuse
edgeCases.expected: One identity-derived entry reused, no copy into releases and no network if needed runtime and control assets are verified cached; no per-release pointer state.

edgeCases.input: Two bootstraps have staged the same official runtime
edgeCases.expected: Only one holds operation.lock at a time; later holder verifies matching complete entry and reuses it. Neither overwrites a conflicting entry nor transfers a lock to final manager.

edgeCases.input: Paths with spaces, apostrophes or Unicode and custom installation homes
edgeCases.expected: Preserve exact quoted argv and explicit home identity in POSIX/PowerShell; no shell-interpolated wire path and canonical local containment enforced.

edgeCases.input: Dev builds invoking npm/npx and native header/library tools
edgeCases.expected: Exact resolved private Node/npm/header paths and existing owned aliases/environment remain; CUDA skip default only if unset, user value preserved; no ambient npm/node/toolchain fallback.

Before publish remove only owned closed stage; after atomic publication preserve verified reusable runtime while ordinary install result may be cancelled. No TUI launch after failed/cancelled install.
No acquisition, source build or full application/Ollama payload rehash; runtime integrity is bounded and verified at process/launch trust boundary, not rescanned by each status/control message.

edgeCases.input: The user explicitly defers Windows and asks to continue macOS/Linux acceptance.
edgeCases.expected: Require actual macOS/Linux foundation proofs and current scoped regression for this handoff. Keep the Windows native subject deferred under ISSUE-cab5701fbefab736, never pass it from an availability diagnostic or POSIX result, and leave Windows enablement disabled.

edgeCases.input: Same-user process changes a runtime or swaps an ancestor between hash and exec
edgeCases.expected: POSIX read-only modes reduce ordinary accidental writes; they do not stop owner chmod, ancestor replacement or pre-existing writable handles. Exact verification rejects later corruption. Hash-to-exec/ancestor races remain accepted within the same-user boundary; no claim of universal OS immutability.

edgeCases.input: Ordinary npm/native build writes next to tooling or headers
edgeCases.expected: Writable npm/node-gyp/header/library inputs are isolated copies under the positively owned build workspace and cleaned only after actor closure. Executing Node remains canonical; copies are checked against the verified source at setup and not treated as a new persistent runtime.

edgeCases.input: TERM/HUP delivered only to the shell PID, or any group signal before the helper is forked
edgeCases.expected: Record the signal without forwarding and wait for exact helper exit. Cancellation can take all remaining helper work, bounded by helper operation deadlines; cleanup remains safe. Prompt abort is tested only when the actual running helper receives the foreground-group signal. No low-latency promise for the shell-only/pre-fork case.

edgeCases.input: Operator considers moving a corrupt runtime while consumers may still be active
edgeCases.expected: Documentation advises stopping every consumer and leaving the entry unchanged if unsure. Product code neither proves shutdown nor holds the native lock for that manual move; it cannot prevent the operator action. No test may claim otherwise. Concurrent-use risk is accepted only through human approval of this design.

edgeCases.input: Cancellation/failure after source-stage permission protection, before successful publication
edgeCases.expected: Restore owner directory write permissions only within the same positively owned closed staging tree to permit discard; use bounded no-follow identity checks and the original stage capability. Uncertain stages and canonical entries stay retained. Never expand stage cleanup into shared-runtime deletion.

alternativesConsidered.name: Manual guidance with narrow read-only protection
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Correct recovery claims and prevent ordinary accidental writes while retaining the isolated writable build SDK.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Recovery remains documentation and a precise runtime-invalid diagnostic: the operator is advised to stop every consumer and preserve the corrupt entry before rerunning the authenticated installer. Product code cannot hold operation.lock or prove consumer closure during that manual action; concurrent-use risk is explicitly accepted, with no enforcement fixture or recovery command. For macOS/Linux, canonical runtime files/directories lose write bits, while official archive/inventory bytes and execute intent remain pinned unchanged. Mutable extraction/SDK workspaces remain separate. The verifier distinguishes source-stage modes from protected canonical modes, rejects writable canonical files, and preserves independent content hashes. Existing intact writable entries can be verified and permission-protected by the existing controller capability without replacing bytes or moving consumers. Corrupt entries stay untouched. Owned-stage cleanup and partial sealing have explicit bounded failure handling. Windows stays deferred.
pros: Stops ordinary accidental file creation/overwrite with EACCES while isolating needed build writes.
No new recovery action or consumer-lifetime protocol; exact diagnostic and accepted manual risk are testable honestly.
Keeps official bytes/inventory hashes and public wire formats unchanged.
cons: Owner can chmod or replace paths; protection is not a hostile same-user boundary.
Manual corrupt-entry movement remains uncoordinated and may disrupt consumers; no product enforcement claim.
Permission-only compatibility and closed-stage cleanup require focused/native qualification.

alternativesConsidered.name: Manual guidance with SDK copy only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Correct recovery wording but retain writable canonical runtime modes.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep LLD6 SDK isolation and current canonical file modes. Remove impossible enforcement/locking claims from manual recovery and its test subject, specify exact diagnostic, and explicitly accept accidental writes outside the copied SDK as well as deliberate same-user writes. No read-only mitigation or recovery command is added.
pros: Smallest contract change; existing mode verifier/profile semantics retained.
No recovery/lifetime protocol or new canonical permission transition.
cons: An accidental write through an absolute canonical path can still disable every shared release.
Only mitigation is known build-input copying; manual uncoordinated recovery risk remains.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Keeps accidental canonical-store writes as an accepted owner risk; it remains a valid narrower alternative pending user choice.

alternativesConsidered.name: Controller-owned runtime recovery command
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Introduce a named recovery control entrypoint and positive consumer coordination.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Design a new authenticated control-bootstrap recovery entrypoint with existing native lock plus independently provable consumer/worker closure, exact entry preservation and reacquisition, dedicated ownership and tests. This would be an explicit recovery action rather than claiming a hand-run procedure enforces those guarantees.
pros: Could make runtime recovery enforcement a real implemented/testable product mechanism.
cons: Requires new consumer-lifetime evidence and lifecycle interactions currently outside this bounded correction.
Needs owner choice and additional design before scope expands; cannot be inferred from feedback.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Requires a new recovery entrypoint and consumer-lifetime mechanism outside this bounded correction without explicit scope choice.

openQuestions: R2-1 owner choice: accept manual-only recovery guidance with no operation.lock or all-consumer shutdown proof/enforcement during an operator move, or request a separately designed control-owned recovery command? Proposed default is manual-only with the exact diagnostic in §4.3.

R2-2 owner choice and rollout: add POSIX read-only protection plus SDK isolation, or retain SDK isolation only and explicitly accept accidental canonical-write risk? Read-only modes change verifier semantics; older control binaries expect original writable modes and can reject protected entries. Mixed-version compatibility is not promised by this draft. Before enabling protection, choose a concrete compatible-controls/rebuild rollout and tests, or choose SDK-only mitigation. Preserve current hostv2; no automatic old-control upgrade is authorized.

erDefinition.narrative: Application releases refer to a shared external runtime identity; the runtime entry owns integrity metadata and executable distribution independently of release cleanup. This documents ownership and many-release-to-one-runtime cardinality without changing public wire fields.

ApplicationRelease.description: Bundle or dev application-only payload with unchanged ReleaseManifest.

runtimeIdentity.description: Unchanged manifest reference to exactly one runtime identity; inverse release membership is shown on RuntimeEntry.

RuntimeEntry.description: One shared runtime identity under an explicit home. Content is immutable to installer code; POSIX write bits are removed to reduce accidental corruption. Owner chmod/pre-opened writable descriptors/path replacement remain outside this protection.

identity.description: Exact version/full target/archive digest/profile key validated against pinned policy.

completion.description: Exactly one completion/inventory metadata set published with the entry.

distribution.description: Exactly one canonical distribution containing verified Node/npm/headers; never app payload bytes.

releases.description: Derived inverse association: one runtime can be referenced by zero or many application releases. This is not a stored runtime-owned release list and does not grant cascade deletion ownership.

RuntimeIntegrity.description: Bounded canonical completion and inventory checked against the independent release-owned policy digest.

inventorySha256.description: Pinned expected distribution inventory digest; arbitrary receipt-supplied hashes are insufficient.

profileVersion.description: Deterministic extraction/profile version shared by bootstrap and resolver.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The first-install bootstrap verifies staged code before it executes, publishes an independent runtime while holding the existing native operation lock, and waits for that exact helper to exit before starting the ordinary manager. Reuse follows the same independent integrity expectations without a second controller or an application payload scan.

participants.label: Shared terminal script
participants.description: POSIX/PowerShell script used by manual invocation and both IDEs; retains terminal I/O.

participants.label: Verified execution stage
participants.description: Owned temporary Node/control bytes authenticated by pinned expected hashes before execution; kept until child exit.

participants.label: Publication helper
participants.description: Minimal trusted control helper; does not select releases or implement daemon lifecycle.

participants.label: Native operation.lock
participants.description: The same exclusive controller lock used by the ordinary manager, never inherited or inferred from PID.

participants.label: External runtime store
participants.description: Canonical runtime entry with pinned content and POSIX read-only publication modes. Permission-only protection of verified compatible entries is controller-owned; corrupt entries get manual guidance only.

participants.label: Final canonical manager
participants.description: Runs under resolved private Node; performs ordinary admission with fresh ownership.

messages.label: Check exact cached executable/control hashes; choose verified reuse or fresh acquisition
messages.description: Cached bytes are checked against release-owned independent expectations, not receipt-supplied executable hashes.

messages.label: Fresh path: download official pinned Node and release control assets; verify before execution
messages.description: Official Node and release-control assets keep their separate fixed origins/digest bindings; archive safety and target checks precede execution.

messages.label: Launch trusted helper using verified staged Node
messages.description: No host Node or release tools/node fallback.

messages.label: Acquire existing native exclusive operation lock
messages.description: Publication is forbidden if another manager owns it.

messages.label: Verify profile and publish separate nonexecuting stage, or verify exact existing entry
messages.description: Windows running node.exe/loaded DLL stay in execution stage; publication is durable and no-replace. On POSIX remove write bits before fresh publication; for existing intact compatible entries verify and protect permissions only, never replace corrupt bytes.

messages.label: Complete policy-bound runtime identity and immutable result
messages.description: No application release selection or hook execution is implied by runtime publication.

messages.label: Actual helper exit observed by its parent
messages.description: Process exit releases helper lock ownership; close(void), record age and PID checks are not substitutes. INT/TERM/HUP are recorded while child active; after exact exit, clear active state and clean only its owned stage, then return signal status. Shell-only signals are not forwarded and can wait for all remaining helper work bounded by its deadlines; do not claim immediate cancellation.

messages.label: OS-hash canonical Node/bootstrap/native immediately before handoff
messages.description: Fresh and cached paths use independent release-owned digests. A residual same-user path/ancestor swap between hash and exec remains an accepted boundary.

messages.label: Start final manager with canonical absolute Node; preserve terminal I/O
messages.description: Do not transfer helper lock handle, session, flag or selected-release authority.

messages.label: Acquire fresh controller ownership and ordinary admission
messages.description: Final manager rechecks current state; concurrent intervening ownership yields normal busy handling.

messages.label: Consume shared read-only runtime resolution
messages.description: Resolver performs no acquisition, application import, DB open or full app/Ollama hash.

componentDependencyDefinition.narrative: Installed consumers share a dependency-minimal resolver. Only acquisition/publication can mutate the external runtime store under the existing controller lock; application releases retain identity metadata and never own runtime bytes.

components.label: Installed control / TUI / Retry consumers
components.description: Existing launch consumers are adapted together; daemon boot remains an S4 consumer of this foundation.

components.label: Verified read-only runtime resolver
components.description: Existing privateRuntimePaths becomes verified async resolution; proposed src/installer/runtime-store.ts contains installer-only implementation.

components.label: Controller-owned acquisition
components.description: Existing bounded acquisition/publication under the original controller capability; no automatic replacement or additional public action.

components.label: Bootstrap publication helper
components.description: Existing helper is adapted to qualified native controller-owned publication and exact-exit handoff.

components.label: External verified runtime entry
components.description: Pinned runtime content with POSIX read-only modes to prevent accidental writes. No security boundary against owner chmod or previously open writable handles; manual corrupt-entry movement is uncoordinated and not product-enforced.

components.label: Bundle/dev application receipt
components.description: Reads application-only format2 receipts with unchanged public RuntimeIdentity metadata.

components.label: Owned writable build SDK
components.description: One ephemeral npm/node-gyp/header/library copy per owned dev build workspace, derived from verified runtime. Node execution remains canonical; cleanup requires positive actor closure.
